subject: Skylab: assembling a station in orbit
one_idea: Three real NASA photographs of Skylab are pinned on an evidence wall and joined by marker lines that read left to right through 1973-74, arguing one station seen by three crews.
facts: Skylab was the United States' first space station; it was occupied in 1973 and re-entered Earth's atmosphere in 1979.
Skylab was visited by three crews: Skylab 2 (1973), Skylab 3 (1973) and Skylab 4 (1973-74).
skylab-rendezvous-flyaround.jpg is NASA image sl2-04-248, photographed during the Skylab 2 rendezvous and fly-around inspection in 1973.
skylab-cluster-black-sky.jpg is NASA image sl3-114-1682, photographed during the Skylab 3 mission in 1973.
skylab-cluster-earth-orbit.jpg is NASA image sl4-143-4707, photographed from the Skylab 4 command and service module in 1974.
All three photographs are works of NASA, a U.S. Government agency, and are in the public domain; the credit line reads "Photographs: NASA (public domain)."
